ratings.label: affiliative
ratings.reason: The message centres on warmth, praise, reassurance and the employee's wellbeing rather than on the task outcome.

ratings.label: authoritative
ratings.reason: It sets out a clear vision of why the work matters and the standard to judge it by, then leaves the means to the employee.

ratings.label: coaching
ratings.reason: It frames the task as a development opportunity, invites self-reflection on strengths and blind spots, and tolerates failure for the sake of learning.

ratings.label: none
ratings.reason: It is a purely administrative description of the brief's structure with no relational or motivational content.

ratings.label: coercive
ratings.reason: It demands strict compliance, rejects the employee's views and threatens replacement and personal blame.

ratings.label: pacesetting
ratings.reason: The manager models high standards, demands speed, refuses guidance and threatens to take over work that falls short.

ratings.label: democratic
ratings.reason: It solicits the employee's ideas and treats their proposals as a vote that shapes the team's direction.
